title: Maternal Smartphone Use and Infant Socioemotional Outcomes: A Differential Susceptibility Perspective
text:
8. PROJECT NARRATIVE
Maternal smartphone use and infant socioemotional outcomes: A differential susceptibility perspective
PI – McDaniel
This longitudinal investigation of maternal smartphone habits around infant caregiving will provide insight into
(a) how maternal smartphone use influences mothers’ emotional well-being, caregiving quality, and infant
socioemotional development during the first year of life, (b) how susceptibility to momentary experiences of
smartphone use may alter the effects, and (c) who is most susceptible to the effects of phone use. Findings
from the proposed research will increase our ability to determine for whom effects are most pronounced to
inform targeted, evidence-based recommendations that optimize parental well-being and infant outcomes.
Thus, findings will have direct relevance to parents and practitioners, assisting mothers with developing
healthier digital habits and improving the quality of caregiving of infants.

title: Neuropathology Core
text: Neuropathology Core Abstract REVISED: The Neuropathology Core (NPC) fulfills several important roles within the University of Pittsburgh ADRC (PITT-ADRC). Postmortem neuropathological confirmation of the clinical diagnosis of Alzheimer’s disease (AD) and related disorders and the assessment of co-existing neurodegenerative and vascular disease processes is essential to promote progress in diagnosis, treatment and prevention of AD. Since its inception, the NPC has collected and characterized 868 brains from PITT-ADRC subjects at various disease stages. This resource has been extensively utilized for teaching purposes and for research studies by local and national investigators to develop amyloid PET imaging agents and correlate in vivo amyloid imaging results with postmortem findings, improve our understanding of genetic factors contributing to AD risk and advance our knowledge regarding the neurobiology of psychiatric comorbidities and neuroinflammatory processes. Our proposed approach to fulfill the diagnostic, tissue banking, research and educational roles of the NPC is outlined in five specific aims: 1) The NPC will continue to maintain and expand a well-catalogued bank of brain tissue samples and fibroblasts of ADRC participants and subjects from affiliated cohorts. A special emphasis will be placed on harvesting brains from subjects with premortem PiB and tau PET imaging studies and perform post-mortem 7T MRI on a select group of participants. 2) All banked cases undergo detailed diagnostic evaluation using the latest consensus criteria and detailed characterization of comorbid and aging-related pathologies. Results will be shared with ADRC clinical staff, families and uploaded to local and national databases (NACC). 3) The NPC will develop, implement and refine novel methods for postmortem tissue characterization such as postmortem MR imaging and digital image analysis algorithms for radiological-to-pathological alignments, quantification of pathology burden and creation of pathology endophenotypes. 4) The NPC will participate in local and national research efforts by providing brain bank tissue materials and neuropathology data from diagnostic evaluations. The NPC will closely collaborate with other PITT-ADRC cores and projects in joint research studies and will engage in NPC-driven research projects. 5) In collaboration with the Research Education Component, the NPC will leverage brain bank materials and expertise to educate neuropathology fellows, residents, medical students and investigators about the neuropathologic features of neurodegenerative diseases. Through these aims, the NPC will provide precise diagnostic classifications of PITT-ADRC research participants, enable studies of phenotype variations and broadly support efforts to improve our understanding of the underlying disease processes.

title: Mitochondrial mechanisms of maternal age effects on offspring health and lifespan
text:
8. PROJECT NARRATIVE/RELEVANCE TO PUBLIC HEALTH
This project will contribute to our understanding of the molecular mechanisms that cause accelerated aging,
decreased health, and shorter lifespan in offspring from older mothers. This study is innovative and significant
in its use of an emerging model system in aging research to examine the role of mitochondrial dysfunction in
maternal age effects on offspring aging. Our work has the potential to identify a cause of interindividual variability
in lifespan and to identify targets for therapies to improve health and increase lifespan.

title: Pathways of Personality Disorder: Combining Multiple Methods of Repeated Assessment Across Development and in Daily Life
text:
Despite the extreme impairments and high economic costs caused by personality disorder (PD), there is a
dearth of research that has investigated the developmental pathways of PD and how they may relate to current
daily functioning. The current study leverages over 17 years of previously collected longitudinal data from the
Preschool Depression Study (PDS) to evaluate how and when core personality processes unfold across
development to predict daily levels of personality functioning in now emerging adults (new data collection using
ecological momentary assessment). Results will elucidate the developmental unfolding and daily manifestation
of core personality processes at the within- and between-person level in young people, thereby allowing for the
identification of targeted early intervention and prevention of PD.

title: Multi-omic CSF Assay for the Diagnosis of Brain Cancers
text:
Belay Diagnostics has developed and validated a highly sensitive and specific multi-omic
technology, CSF-TumorDx, that can detect tumor derived DNA in cerebrospinal fluid to
aid in the diagnosis of brain cancers. In this Fast-Track application we will: i) establish
pre-analytic quality control procedures, ii) determine the analytical sensitivity and
specificity of CSF-TumorDx and iii) determine the clinical validity of CSF-TumorDx.
Belay Diagnostics will work closely with investigators at the Johns Hopkins University
School of Medicine to validate the performance of CSF-TumorDx and at the completion
of this proposal will have a CLIA certified test ready for clinical implementation and
commercialization.

title: Role of Mitochondrial Metabolism in Regulating Species-Specific Developmental Rates
text:
Although mammalian species display significant variation in the rate of embryonic development, the
mechanisms that define species-specific developmental rates remain unknown. The proposed research
program will leverage in vitro models of mouse and human development to define the role of mitochondrial
metabolism in regulating developmental speed. Elucidating the mechanisms that control developmental rate
will enable its direct manipulation, making possible the acceleration of human induced pluripotent stem cell
differentiation for disease modeling and cell-based therapies.

title: Fatty acid metabolism regulates ferroptosis in mutant KRAS lung cancer
text:
Mutant KRAS ( K M ) is the most common oncogenic mutation of lung cancer. We determined that in
 lung cancer KM establishes a critical dependency on fatty acid synthase (FASN), the enzyme that
 catalyzes the synthesis of saturated long chain fatty acids.
 In this proposal, we will test the innovative hypothesis that FASN exerts a pro-survival function by providing
fatty acids to feed the Lands cycle, the main cellular process that deflect ferroptosis, a form of programmed cell
death. We anticipate that our findings will provide unanticipated insights into KM-driven tumorigenesis,
unravelling novel therapeutic venues.

title: UCSC Graduate Program in Genome Sciences
text:
The UCSC Graduate Program in Genome Science is designed to train the next generation of scientific leaders
in genome sciences, a discipline that is critical to development of new therapies—from cancer to heritable
disease. UCSC has been a leader in genomics research since the field was founded and offers a rich
interdisciplinary genomics training environment. Our program spans 26 training faculty from 8 departments and
combines formal training in statistics, programming, and engineering with more traditional disciplines, such as
molecular biology and genetics.

title: Core B: Biospecimen Repository
text:
Through the work of the MSK SPORE in Prostate Cancer, supported by the Biospecimen Repository Core, we
hope to increase our understanding of the clinical, biologic, and genetic basis of prostate cancer to improve
patient outcomes; to facilitate a range of scientific activities that could lead to new genomic- and proteomic-
based interventions for cancer, including target identification and validation; and to develop new biomarkers,
diagnostics, and pharmacogenomic analyses.

title: Virtual Activities of Living for Occupational Rehabilitation
text:
The proposed VALOR system consists of mobile virtual world software that enables functional practice of
immersive ADLs and IADLs for upper extremity (UE) stroke rehabilitation using a low-cost, untethered,
standalone VR headset with computer vision-based, markerless hand tracking. The proposed SBIR Phase II
research addresses important public health concerns by: (1) enabling low-cost delivery of evidence-based care
through telehealth; (2) improving stroke outcomes in UE function by enabling increased frequency and intensity
of practice; (3) providing reliable tracking mechanisms for patient activity, functional status, and progress; and
(4) increasing access to underserved populations and areas through cost-effective, independent home use with
teletherapy support.

title: The role of IL-6/STAT3 signaling in CIC-DUX4 fusion sarcoma metastasis and immunosuppression
text:
We will define the underlying biological mechanisms by which IL-6/STAT3 signaling drives CIC-
DUX4 fusion-mediated sarcoma progression/metastasis and immunosuppression. Through these
mechanistic studies, our goals are to identify novel therapeutic targets to build the foundation for
developing potent immune-based therapies that will improve outcomes for CIC-DUX4 fusion-positive
patients.

title: tRNA modification reprogramming and translational remodeling in cancer
text:
More than 100,000 new cases of melanoma will be diagnosed in the USA this year and the 5-year survival rate
is only 35% when it spreads to distant organs. Therefore, a better understanding of mechanisms of melanoma
metastasis is therefore urgently needed. We will investigate the role of tRNA modifications and tRNA-modifying
enzymes in the context of melanoma and metastasis.

title: Project 2 - Ex Vivo Analysis of Coronavirus Tropism, Adaptation, Replication, and Host Response
text: PROJECT 2: Ex Vivo Analysis of Coronavirus Tropism, Adaptation, Replication, and Host Response In this proposal, we hypothesize that multiple and discrete virus-host interactions and host responses to infection dictate the pathogenic outcome and host tropism of SARS-CoV-2. We further hypothesize that these critical circuits can be dissected through network-based modeling of system-level measurements offering the potential for the development of novel antiviral therapies. In Project 2, we propose to utilize leading edge OMICs- based measurements to define virus-host interactions and networks that control viral replication, viral tropism/adaptation and host responses across bat coronaviruses, SARS-CoV-1, and SARS-CoV-2 variants. In Aim 1, we will conduct proteomics (AP-MS, protein abundance and post-translational modifications), transcriptomics (RNA-seq and scRNA-seq), epigenomics (ATAC-seq, Hi-C and ChiP-seq) and genetic and chemical compound screens using ex vivo primary epithelial cells and iPSC-derived pneumocytes derived both from human and bats and a lung epithelial cell line (A549). In Aim 2, these data will be integrated and modeled with in vivo and clinical data collected in Project 1 using network-based predictive modeling approaches to identify host proteins, networks, and pathways that correlate with disease severity and host adaptation (‘driver genes’). Reiterative modeling of data generated in Aim 1 and Project 1 will be employed to refine these predictions. In Aim 3, CRISPR-editing approaches will be used in concert with targeted OMICs measurements (CRISPR-OMICs), including transcriptional, epigenetic, proteomic analyses, to validate the impact of these ‘driver genes’ on disease outcome and host tropism. Additional molecular, cellular, biochemical, and in vivo studies will be conducted to further characterize nodes that determine disease outcome as potential therapeutic targets. Overall, these studies will enable us to correlate in vivo and clinical biomarkers predictive of COVID-19 severity (Project 1) to specific genes and networks that impact viral infection, cellular host responses, and interspecies transmission.

title: Center for Cancer Control in Persistent Poverty Areas (C3P2)
text:
OVERALL NARRATIVE
In collaboration with residents and representatives of communities living in Persistent Poverty in Alabama, the
University of Alabama at Birmingham (UAB)'s Center for Cancer Control in Persistent Poverty Areas
(C3P2) will build a research program and research capacity to improve cancer prevention and control in these
communities. Starting from nine urban Persistent Poverty Census Tracts identified as such by the NCI, the
C3P2 goal is to support transdisciplinary multi-level research to address Social Determinants of Health, in
particular addressing poor living environments, and to provide efficacious adapted interventions to enhance
health promotion and adoption of healthy behaviors across the cancer continuum from prevention to
survivorship.

title: Carbohydrate-Mediated Platelet Clearance
text:
Signals communicating the need to maintain balanced blood production and aged blood cell removal must be
correctly conveyed to the marrow's hematopoietic stem and progenitor cells and covey proper blood cell removal
signals. These molecular mechanisms are intensely studied to provide new insight into the potential for novel
therapeutic approaches in blood disorders, specifically affecting platelet and red blood cell counts. The proposed
work will yield a transformative understanding of how liver-produced factors contribute to maintaining red blood
cell production in the bone marrow at a steady state and provide new insight into novel therapeutic approaches
for patients with blood disorders.

title: Postdoctoral Training in Cardiovascular Disease
text:
Our training program seeks to train physicians and surgeons in the design and execution
of high-quality clinically relevant cardiovascular research. The program is designed to
enhance and ensure the development of academic leaders by acquiring broad-based
scientific knowledge. Highly qualified applicants have filled the slots within the training
program.

title: Glutamine metabolism and vesicant pathogenesis
text:
Chemical warfare vesicant exposure leads to increased oxidative stress and cytotoxicity, yet how vesicants
affect metabolism to induce pathogenesis is understudied. We will uncover the overlapping metabolic
pathways disrupted by vesicant exposure as well as understand whether glutamine metabolism has a
protective role in both preclinical and human tissue models. Our findings will have significant public health
implications, offering potential insights to inform effective treatments and countermeasures for individuals
affected by chemical warfare exposure, ultimately contributing to improved health outcomes and emergency
response strategies.

title: Epigenetic mechanisms of anhedonia and fear in AUD
text:
Research Project 3: Project Narrative
This proposal within the Center for Alcohol Research in Epigenetics (CARE) will determine if cell-type specific
epigenetic mechanisms induced during withdrawal from chronic alcohol drinking in rats alter neuroimmune gene
expression and neuronal function within the hippocampus. They will also determine if these mechanisms regulate
withdrawal-induced increases in behaviors associated with comorbid disorders depression, panic disorder and
PTSD. Results from these projects will improve our understanding of alcohol use disorder and its comorbidities,
and lead to new epigenetic targets for treatment.

title: Investigating mechanisms of CARD11 mutants in enhanced anti-tumor immunity and T cell fitness (For Kathleen Cheng)
text:
Adoptive cellular therapies have limited efficacy in solid tumors which account for 90% of adult
cancers. The CARD protein-BCL10-MALT1 signaling complex is an essential mediator of T cell
activation, and the novel CARD11-PIK3R3 fusion identified by our group has demonstrated robust
and dramatic anti-tumor efficacy in vivo. This proposal aims to understand the mechanisms by which
CARD11-PIK3R3 improves T cell fitness and anti-tumor efficacy in order to advance our
understanding of T cell biology, elucidate mechanisms to engineer more effective T cell therapies,
and ultimately provide more efficacious treatment options for patients.

title: Identification and characterization of mCpH binding proteins in neurons
text:
CpH (H=A/C/T) methylation was found high level in neurons and plays important roles in brain development
and neurological disorders. Using a state-of-the-art protein array, Digital Affinity Profiling via Proximity Ligation
(DAPPL), a viral in vivo delivery system and high-throughput sequencing technologies, we will identify
sequence-independent and -dependent mCpH-binding proteins and characterize their roles in transcriptional
and chromatin regulation in adult mouse brain. These data will provide a foundation to investigate the roles of
CpH methylation in brain disorders.
